title: How the Python SDK builds a request: body and query key casing, ID lists

prose.text: The Python SDK takes snake_case arguments and rewrites key names before a request goes out; which keys it rewrites depends on the service and the client.

prose.label: Request bodies.
prose.text: {{body-camel-case}} {{camel-rule}} Product-specific consequences: ZIA's exceptions in [[zia.sdk-python.request-conventions:camel-case-body]], ZCC's in [[zcc.api.conventions:python-body-casing]], ZTB's in [[zero-trust-branch.api:snake-case-bodies]].

prose.label: Query parameters.
prose.text: {{query-params-camel-case}} ZPA's own page-size and search handling is in [[zpa.sdk-python.pagination]].

prose.label: ID lists.
prose.text: {{id-list-helper}} Which keys ZIA reshapes this way is in [[zia.sdk-python.request-conventions:id-list-reshape]].

body-camel-case.statement: For a dictionary request body, the request executor camel-cases the keys with `convert_keys_to_camel_case`, except on the ZDX and ZTB legacy clients and on endpoints containing `/zdx/`, `/easm/` or `/ztb/`, whose bodies it sends as given. For `/zcc/` it converts selectively, leaving `WebPolicy.SNAKE_CASE_KEYS` as they are, and a body the ZCC serializer already produced (`_ZccWireBody`) is sent unchanged.

quotes: return body  # Do not convert anything, just return as-is
return body  # Do not convert ZDX requests to camelCase
return body  # Do not convert ZEASM requests to camelCase
return body  # Do not convert ZTB requests to camelCase
# Preserve existing logic for other services

query-params-camel-case.statement: For every service other than ZPA, the request executor camel-cases query parameter names with `convert_keys_to_camel_case` and removes `microtenantId`; on the ZDX legacy client it leaves the parameters as given.

quotes: # Normal param conversion if not ZPA

camel-rule.statement: The camel-casing helper returns a key from its exceptions table as mapped and leaves a key without an underscore unchanged; otherwise it splits on underscores, lowercases the first part, capitalizes every later part and joins them.

quotes: if string in FIELD_EXCEPTIONS: return FIELD_EXCEPTIONS[string]
if not string or "_" not in string: return string

id-list-helper.statement: `transform_common_id_fields` pops each snake_case key from the source dict and stores a list of `{"id": ...}` objects under the wire key; items that are already dicts with an id are kept.
